chemicals.concentration_notes: The overall toxicity and potency of the Peruvian Lily are considered very mild12. Interestingly, the Peruvian Lily was listed among the top 10 cat exposure calls to the Pet Poison Helpline in 2023; this is largely because it is incredibly common in floral bouquets and the name "lily" causes immediate panic for cat owners.
chemicals.description: Tulipalin A (alpha-methylene-gamma-butyrolactone) and its precursor tuliposide A act as chemical irritants. When a cat chews or swallows the plant material, these compounds irritate the gastrointestinal tract, resulting in minor signs such as mild, self-limiting stomach upset. Because the Peruvian Lily (Alstroemeria spp.) is an "imposter lily" and not a true Lilium, it does not cause the acute, fatal kidney failure seen with Easter or Tiger lilies.
chemicals.name: Tulipalin A / Tuliposide A

description:
Peruvian Lily (Alstroemeria spp.) is a common flower in bouquets that is only mildly irritating to cats. Because it has "lily" in its name, it often causes panic, but it is not a true lily and does not cause dangerous kidney failure like Easter or Tiger lilies do.

The plant contains a chemical irritant called tulipalin A (and its precursor tuliposide A) throughout its tissues. If a cat chews on the leaves or stems, this compound can irritate the mouth and upset the stomach. The sap can also cause some redness or itching if it gets directly on the skin (the same compound behind "tulip fingers" in florists).

Most cats will only experience minor drooling, vomiting, or diarrhea that goes away on its own. While it is safer than many other plants, it is best to keep bouquets out of reach. Contact a veterinarian if your cat eats a large amount or if their stomach upset does not improve.

name: Peruvian Lily
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: tulipalin A and its precursor tuliposide A (an irritant glycoside) throughout the plant; not related to the nephrotoxic compounds in true Lilium species
Mechanism: GI irritant; sap contact causes dermatitis through direct tissue irritation
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, drooling; skin or eye contact with sap may cause redness and irritation
No kidney failure risk — a critical difference from Easter and Tiger lilies
Symptoms are mild and self-limiting; contact your vet if ingestion was significant or symptoms persist

symptoms.name: Stomach upset (vomiting and/or diarrhea)
symptoms.notes: The stomach upset caused by Peruvian lilies is considered minor and self-limiting13. Because Peruvian lilies are not "true" lilies, they do not cause acute kidney failure, and actual poisoning is rare despite the plant's frequent appearance in floral bouquets.

symptoms.name: Minor signs of oral toxicity or irritation
symptoms.notes: This minor irritation is caused by tulipalin A (and its precursor tuliposide A) present in the plant, a chemical irritant that affects the tissues when the cat chews on the plant material.
symptoms.onset: Immediate to shortly after chewing the plant.

treatments.description: In the rare event of significant oral or throat irritation, the veterinarian will monitor the cat for tissue swelling. If swelling were to obstruct breathing, the vet will secure the airway and provide supplemental oxygen.
treatments.name: Securing an Airway and Oxygen Support
treatments.notes: This is an emergency measure that is rarely necessary, but it is the most critical priority if severe swelling occurs.

treatments.description: The mouth is wiped out to physically remove any remaining plant material and irritant sap. The oral cavity is then rinsed with water to help clear away residual tulipalin A and ease irritation.
treatments.name: Removal of Plant Material and Oral Rinsing
treatments.notes: Rinsing the mouth and offering water helps dilute and clear the irritant sap, easing the cat's discomfort.

treatments.description: The cat is observed for mild, self-limiting stomach upset, excessive drooling, or oral pain24. Basic supportive care is provided until the irritation naturally subsides.
treatments.name: General Supportive Care and Monitoring
treatments.notes: Because Peruvian lilies only cause mild, localized irritation, there is no concern for systemic organ injury or renal failure24. Full recovery is expected, and many cats recover completely at home without requiring a clinic visit.
